description: Haemul Pajeon is a beloved crispy Korean savory pancake packed with a delightful medley of fresh seafood and vibrant green onions. This classic dish offers a perfect balance of chewy textures from the seafood and a satisfying crunch from its golden-brown exterior. It's an incredibly flavorful and comforting dish, ideal as an appetizer, snack, or light meal.

instructions.title: Prepare the Seafood
instructions.text: Clean and prepare all seafood. Shrimp should be peeled, deveined, and roughly chopped. Squid should be cleaned and sliced into rings or small pieces. Pat all seafood dry with paper towels to remove excess moisture.

instructions.title: Make the Batter
instructions.text: In a large bowl, whisk together all-purpose flour, rice flour, salt, and black pepper. Gradually add cold water and the egg, whisking until a smooth, thin batter forms. Be careful not to overmix; a few lumps are fine.

instructions.title: Combine Ingredients
instructions.text: Add the prepared seafood, green onions, and sliced onion to the batter. Gently mix to ensure all ingredients are coated.

instructions.title: Heat the Pan
instructions.text: Heat 2 tablespoons of vegetable oil in a large non-stick skillet or cast-iron pan over medium-high heat until shimmering.

instructions.title: Cook the First Side
instructions.text: Pour about half of the batter mixture into the hot pan, spreading it evenly to form a round pancake. Arrange any additional green onion pieces or red chili slices on top if desired. Cook for 5-7 minutes until the bottom is golden brown and crispy.

instructions.title: Flip and Finish Cooking
instructions.text: Carefully flip the pancake. Add another tablespoon of oil around the edges if needed. Press down gently with a spatula to ensure even cooking. Cook for another 5-7 minutes until the second side is golden brown and the seafood is cooked through.

instructions.title: Prepare Dipping Sauce
instructions.text: While the pancakes cook, whisk together soy sauce, rice vinegar, sesame oil, sesame seeds, minced garlic, and a pinch of red pepper flakes in a small bowl.

instructions.title: Serve Immediately
instructions.text: Transfer the cooked Haemul Pajeon to a cutting board, slice into wedges, and serve immediately with the prepared dipping sauce. Repeat steps 5 and 6 for the remaining batter to make a second pancake.

tips: Use very cold water for the batter; it helps create a crispier pancake. You can even use sparkling water for an extra light texture.
Don't overcrowd the pan. Cook in batches if your pan isn't large enough, or make two smaller pancakes for easier flipping.
For extra crispiness, use more oil than you think you need, especially when flipping. The oil helps fry the edges to a perfect crunch.
article:
Haemul Pajeon: The Ultimate Guide to Korean Seafood Pancake

Imagine a sizzling hot plate arriving at your table, steam rising gently, revealing a golden-brown, crispy-edged pancake studded generously with vibrant green onions and an array of succulent seafood. This, my friends, is Haemul Pajeon – a culinary masterpiece from Korea that has captured hearts and palates worldwide. More than just a pancake, it’s a celebration of fresh ingredients, textures, and flavors, offering a delightful crunch followed by a tender, savory interior. Whether enjoyed as a comforting snack, a vibrant appetizer, or a perfect accompaniment to a cold drink, Haemul Pajeon promises an unforgettable gastronomic experience. If you're looking for an authentic Haemul Pajeon Recipe to recreate this magic at home, you've come to the right place.

## What is Haemul Pajeon?

Haemul Pajeon literally translates to "seafood green onion pancake." "Haemul" means seafood, and "Pajeon" refers to a pancake primarily made with green onions ("pa"). This iconic Korean dish stands out from other jeon (Korean savory pancakes) due to its generous use of fresh seafood and the distinctive, sweet-yet-sharp flavor of green onions. Unlike Western pancakes, pajeon is savory and typically thinner, designed to achieve a wonderfully crispy exterior while maintaining a soft, chewy inside. It’s a staple in Korean households, a popular street food, and a must-order at izakayas (Korean pubs) where it's often paired with makgeolli (Korean rice wine) or soju. The beauty of Haemul Pajeon lies in its simplicity yet profound depth of flavor – the umami from the seafood, the freshness of the green onions, and the satisfying crispness of the batter all come together in perfect harmony.

## Ingredients for Haemul Pajeon

Gathering the right ingredients is the first step to a successful Haemul Pajeon Recipe. While the concept is simple, the quality of your components will significantly impact the final taste and texture.

For the Batter:
*   1 cup all-purpose flour (or Korean pancake mix for extra crispiness)
*   1/2 cup cold water or anchovy broth (broth adds more depth of flavor)
*   1 large egg
*   1/2 teaspoon salt
*   Pinch of black pepper

For the Filling:
*   1 bunch (about 8-10 stalks) green onions, trimmed and cut into 2-3 inch lengths
*   1/2 cup shrimp, peeled, deveined, and roughly chopped
*   1/2 cup squid, cleaned and thinly sliced into rings or small pieces
*   1/4 cup mussels or clams, shelled (optional, but adds great flavor)
*   1/4 small onion, thinly sliced (optional, for added sweetness)
*   1-2 fresh red or green chilies, thinly sliced (optional, for a kick)

For Frying:
*   Vegetable oil or any neutral cooking oil, generously

For the Dipping Sauce (essential!):
*   2 tablespoons soy sauce
*   1 tablespoon rice vinegar
*   1 teaspoon sesame oil
*   1 teaspoon toasted sesame seeds
*   1/2 teaspoon gochugaru (Korean chili flakes), optional
*   1 clove garlic, minced (optional)

Ensure your seafood is fresh or properly thawed. The green onions should be vibrant and crisp. If using Korean pancake mix, adjust the water content according to package directions, as it often contains seasoning and leavening agents for optimal crispiness.

## How to Make Haemul Pajeon: Step-by-Step

Creating this delicious Korean seafood pancake is easier than you might think. Follow these steps for a foolproof Haemul Pajeon Recipe that will impress your family and friends.

1.  **Prepare Your Ingredients:** Clean and prepare all your seafood. Pat them dry with paper towels to prevent the batter from becoming watery. Cut green onions into 2-3 inch pieces. If using, thinly slice the onion and chilies.
2.  **Make the Batter:** In a large mixing bowl, whisk together the flour, cold water (or broth), egg, salt, and pepper until just combined. A few lumps are okay; overmixing can lead to a tough pancake. The batter should be slightly thick but pourable, similar to a thin pancake batter.
3.  **Combine Filling with Batter:** Add the prepared seafood, most of the green onions (reserve a handful for topping), sliced onion, and chilies (if using) into the batter. Gently fold to coat all the ingredients evenly.
4.  **Heat the Pan:** Heat a large non-stick skillet or cast-iron pan over medium-high heat. Add a generous amount of vegetable oil – enough to coat the bottom of the pan and come up the sides slightly (about 2-3 tablespoons). The oil is crucial for achieving that characteristic crispy crust.
5.  **Cook the Pancake:** Once the oil is hot (it should shimmer slightly), pour about half of the batter into the pan, spreading it evenly to form a round pancake about 1/2 to 3/4 inch thick. Immediately arrange the reserved green onion pieces on top of the batter, pressing them gently.
6.  **Sear and Crisp:** Cook for 4-6 minutes on the first side, or until the bottom is golden brown and crispy, and the edges begin to curl up. You should see bubbles forming on the surface.
7.  **Flip and Cook Second Side:** Carefully, using a large spatula, flip the pancake over. Add a little more oil around the edges of the pan if it looks dry. Cook for another 3-5 minutes on the second side until golden brown and cooked through. Press down gently with the spatula to ensure even contact with the pan.
8.  **Repeat:** If your pan isn't large enough for all the batter, repeat the process for the remaining batter, adding more oil as needed.
9.  **Make the Dipping Sauce:** While the pancake is cooking, whisk together all the dipping sauce ingredients in a small bowl.
10. **Serve Immediately:** Transfer the cooked Haemul Pajeon to a cutting board. Slice it into wedges or squares and serve hot with the dipping sauce on the side.

## Tips for the Perfect Korean Seafood Pancake

Achieving that ideal balance of crispy exterior and tender interior in your Haemul Pajeon Recipe requires a few key techniques.

*   **Cold Water/Broth:** Using very cold water or broth for the batter helps create a crispier texture by inhibiting gluten development.
*   **Don't Overmix the Batter:** Lumps are your friend here. Overmixing develops gluten, leading to a chewy, rather than crispy, pancake.
*   **Generous Oil is Key:** Don't be shy with the oil! It's essential for achieving a deep golden color and a wonderfully crispy crust. You can even add a little more oil around the edges after flipping to ensure the second side gets equally crisp.
*   **High Heat to Start:** Begin with medium-high heat to quickly crisp up the exterior. You can reduce it slightly once flipped to ensure the interior cooks through without burning the outside.
*   **Don't Overcrowd the Pan:** Cook one large pancake or two smaller ones at a time, depending on your pan size. Overcrowding lowers the pan temperature and prevents proper browning.
*   **Pat Seafood Dry:** Excess moisture from the seafood can make the batter soggy. A quick pat with paper towels helps keep things crisp.
*   **Use a Korean Pancake Mix:** If you want an extra crispy and flavorful result, try using a specific Korean pancake mix (buchim garu). It often contains rice flour and other starches designed for optimal crispness.

## Serving Suggestions & Dipping Sauce

A Haemul Pajeon Recipe isn't complete without its quintessential dipping sauce. This tangy, savory, and slightly spicy condiment perfectly complements the richness of the pancake.

The dipping sauce, typically a simple blend of soy sauce, rice vinegar, sesame oil, and sesame seeds, cuts through the richness of the pancake and adds a burst of flavor. You can customize it with a pinch of gochugaru (Korean chili flakes) for a subtle kick, or minced garlic for an aromatic punch.

Serve your Haemul Pajeon fresh off the pan, cut into bite-sized wedges or squares. It's truly best enjoyed hot and crispy. In Korea, it's a popular anju (food served with alcohol), especially with makgeolli, whose slight fizziness and sweetness beautifully contrast the savory pancake. It also makes a fantastic appetizer for any Korean meal or a delightful main course on its own.

## Variations & Substitutions

While the classic Haemul Pajeon Recipe is a star, its versatility allows for delicious variations and substitutions to suit different tastes and dietary needs.

*   **Vegetable Pajeon (Yachaejeon):** Omit the seafood entirely and load up on other vegetables like thinly sliced carrots, bell peppers, mushrooms, zucchini, or even kimchi for Kimchi Pajeon.
*   **Meat Additions:** For a heartier pancake, you can add thinly sliced beef (bulgogi style) or pork to the batter.
*   **Different Seafood:** Feel free to experiment with other types of seafood like oysters, baby octopus, or a mix of various shellfishes. Just ensure they are cut into small, manageable pieces that cook quickly.
*   **Flour Alternatives:** While all-purpose flour is standard, you can experiment with a portion of glutinous rice flour or cornstarch for added chewiness and crispness.
*   **Spicy Kick:** Besides gochugaru in the dipping sauce, you can add finely chopped fresh green or red chilies directly into the batter for an internal heat.

With this comprehensive Haemul Pajeon Recipe, you're ready to create a culinary masterpiece that brings the vibrant flavors of Korea right into your kitchen. Enjoy the process, and savor every crispy, savory bite!
